title: Secretly recorded conversation with then-wife Judit Varga about the Schadl–Völner case files
description: After breaking with Fidesz in February 2024, Magyar was heard as a witness by the Budapest Investigating Prosecutor's Office on 20 March 2024 in the Schadl–Völner bribery case and told the press he could prove that people around cabinet minister Antal Rogán had manipulated the investigation files. On 26 March 2024 he published a roughly two-minute recording of a January 2023 conversation in which Judit Varga, then justice minister and his wife, says that Rogán's circle had passages removed from the case files. Magyar made the recording without Varga's knowledge. Varga said she had made the statements because Magyar was intimidating her and that he had used the recording to blackmail her; Magyar rejected this and accused her of defamation. The episode made Magyar a national political figure; no criminal proceedings against him over the recording were reported in the sources consulted.
key_facts: 20 March 2024: about four hours of witness testimony at the Budapest Investigating Prosecutor's Office (Fővárosi Nyomozó Ügyészség)
26 March 2024: publication of the January 2023 recording in which Varga refers to Rogán's people having names removed from the case files
The recording was made without Varga's knowledge; Varga said her statements were made under pressure
Magyar denied Varga's account and called her statement defamatory

title: Domestic-abuse allegations by former justice minister Judit Varga
description: On 26 March 2024, the day Magyar released the recording, his former wife Judit Varga, who had resigned as an MP in February 2024 and had been justice minister until 2023, publicly accused him of verbal and physical abuse during their marriage and of having pressured her. Magyar denied the accusations, called them defamation and said they had been prepared by the government side to divert attention from the recording. In July 2025, when she appeared as a witness in the bribery trial in which her former deputy at the justice ministry is a defendant, Varga publicly repeated the accusations of violence and blackmail and called his conduct a 'betrayal' of their family; Magyar said he would not respond to 'repeated propaganda'. According to the reporting consulted, no criminal proceedings have been brought against Magyar over these allegations; he is entitled to the presumption of innocence.
key_facts: Accusations first made publicly by Varga on 26 March 2024
Magyar denies them and calls them defamatory
Varga repeated the accusations in July 2025
No criminal case against Magyar reported in the sources consulted

title: Ötkert nightclub incident and the phone dropped into the Danube (June 2024)
description: In the early hours of 21 June 2024, less than two weeks after the European Parliament election, Magyar was involved in a scuffle at the Ötkert club in central Budapest, of which several videos circulated. According to the Prosecutor General's Office, he took the mobile phone of a man who was filming him and deliberately dropped it into the Danube, conduct the prosecution said in September 2024 could amount to theft. Magyar called the case an attempt at political character assassination and said in September 2026 that he would act the same way again to protect young people he said had been attacked. Pro-government outlets published claims that he had harassed women at the club; Magyar sued and, by September 2024, had won eight press-correction cases about the Ötkert reporting. The criminal side of the case is recorded in the justice section.
key_facts: Incident in the early hours of 21 June 2024 at the Ötkert club, Budapest
Prosecutors' position (September 2024): taking the phone could constitute theft
European Parliament declined to lift his immunity in October 2025; the Hungarian parliament lifted it at his own request on 28 September 2026
Courts ordered several pro-government outlets to correct claims that he had harassed women at the club

title: Walk-out from a live ATV interview (June 2024)
description: On 10 June 2024, the day after the European Parliament election, Magyar left the studio of ATV's 'Egyenes Beszéd' programme about one and a half minutes into a live interview, after presenter Egon Rónai confronted him with a list of the channel's invitations to counter his complaints that ATV had not invited him. Magyar said the channel was linked to the governing camp and called the exchange a prepared provocation; ATV issued a statement rejecting his claims.
key_facts: Live interview on 10 June 2024, ended by Magyar after about 90 seconds
Dispute over how often ATV had invited him during the campaign
Magyar called it a provocation; ATV published a statement in response

title: 'Tisza tax' documents and the Tisza Party's press-correction lawsuits
description: From August 2025 the news site Index published articles, based on documents it said were leaked Tisza materials, claiming that the party was preparing large income-tax increases and austerity; government politicians and a government 'national consultation' relied on them during the campaign. Magyar called the documents forgeries. The Tisza Party, of which Magyar is president, filed four press-correction suits against Index and nine against outlets that republished the claims. According to fact-checker Lakmusz (March 2026), courts had ruled for Tisza in several cases at first or second instance, while second-instance rulings in favour of Magyar Nemzet and Ripost held that the reports were protected political opinion; no court had ruled on the documents' authenticity. The plaintiff in these cases is the Tisza Party; Magyar is not personally a party to them.
key_facts: Index articles of 26 August 2025 and 25 November 2025 on alleged Tisza tax plans
13 press-correction suits brought by the Tisza Party (4 against Index, 9 against republishing outlets)
Mixed outcomes; several cases pending at second instance or before the Kúria as of March 2026
Magyar is not personally a party to these proceedings

title: Nomination of his brother-in-law as justice minister (April–May 2026)
description: On about 30 April 2026 Magyar announced that Márton Melléthei-Barna, a lawyer and Tisza MP who had married Magyar's sister in September 2025, would be justice minister in his government. The choice drew accusations of nepotism. On the evening of 7 May 2026, two days before the new parliament's inaugural sitting, Melléthei-Barna withdrew, saying he wanted to avoid any appearance of nepotism so that the new government could start with a clean slate; he remained an MP. Márta Görög was nominated instead.
key_facts: Nomination announced about a week before the withdrawal
Withdrawal on 7 May 2026 citing the appearance of nepotism
Márta Görög appointed Minister of Justice instead

title: Ending President Tamás Sulyok's term by constitutional amendment (2026)
description: In his election-night speech on 12 April 2026 Magyar called on President Tamás Sulyok, the chief prosecutor and the heads of several state bodies appointed under Orbán to resign. Sulyok refused and turned to the Council of Europe's Venice Commission, alleging a constitutional crisis. Tisza's two-thirds majority then adopted the 17th amendment to the Fundamental Law in July 2026 (139 votes to 6), which ended the president's mandate; Sulyok signed it on 18 July 2026, saying the rule of law and the separation of powers had been 'trampled' for reasons of power, and his term ended on 20 July. Parliament elected former Supreme Court president András Baka as president on 11 August 2026 while Fidesz boycotted the vote. Fidesz and the KDNP called the removal 'tyrannical' and 'illegitimate'; Magyar argued it was part of the 'system change' voters had endorsed.
key_facts: 17th amendment to the Fundamental Law adopted in July 2026 by 139 votes to 6
Sulyok signed on 18 July 2026; his mandate ended on 20 July 2026
András Baka elected president on 11 August 2026 (140 to 6), Fidesz boycotting
Criticism from Fidesz–KDNP

title: Suspension of public-media news and overhaul of MTVA (2026)
description: On 15 April 2026, in tense interviews on public radio and television, prime minister-elect Magyar called the public broadcaster a 'propaganda machine', compared its coverage to propaganda from North Korea and Nazi-era Germany, and said his government would suspend its news services until their public-service character was restored; the state media authority rejected his claim that he had been shut out of public media during the campaign. Parliament adopted a public-media reform in June 2026 (145 votes to 39, with Fidesz–KDNP against) that replaced MTVA and Duna Média and required their leadership to step down, and on 7 July 2026 the new interim management took M1 off air and suspended news across public media, broadcasting an apology for past coverage. The government presented the step as ending state propaganda; Fidesz opposed the reform. According to MTVA, M1 had previously shown a black screen only during technical problems or national mourning.
key_facts: Pledge to suspend public-media news repeated after the 12 April 2026 election
Public-media reform adopted in June 2026 by 145 votes to 39
7 July 2026: M1 off air and news suspended; news reintroduced from 20 August 2026 according to State Media Monitor

title: Selection of the head of the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (August 2026)
description: The law creating the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH), a central anti-corruption pledge, was criticised in draft form by the Hungarian Helsinki Committee for giving the office unduly broad discretion and excluding judicial review of its investigations, and Fidesz called the office a 'Tisza ÁVH' (after the communist-era secret police) and announced a Constitutional Court challenge. On 28 August 2026 the Tisza majority elected political scientist Anna Unger as its head (137 votes to 7, 1 abstention), most Fidesz and KDNP MPs having left the chamber. Former independent MP Ákos Hadházy questioned the selection among 94 applicants, alleging without published evidence that it had been a 'charade' and a compromise between Magyar and minister Bálint Ruff, and asked for the scoring to be released; Fidesz called Unger a 'political commissar' without practical experience.
key_facts: Helsinki Committee (June 2026) criticised the draft law's limited judicial review
Anna Unger elected head on 28 August 2026 for six years from 1 September
Fidesz announced a Constitutional Court challenge against the law
Hadházy requested the scoring of the 94 applications, alleging an arranged choice
